name: Lionel Johnson
bio: Poet and critic (1867-1902), a Winchester and New College man, a friend and great admirer of Walter Pater, and a member of the Rhymers' Club alongside Yeats, Dowson and Symons. Wilde called on him unannounced at Oxford in February 1890 because he admired his poems; two days later Johnson wrote to a friend, 'I am in love with him'. In 1891 he brought his Winchester contemporary Lord Alfred Douglas to Tite Street and introduced them. In 1892 he wrote 'The Destroyer of a Soul', believed addressed to Wilde, which begins 'I hate you with a necessary hate'. He died at thirty-five.
